newsitem.title: USA: Travelers Q4 life insurance earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Travelers Q4 life insurance earnings up.

text.p: Travelers Group Inc said its Travelers Life & Annuity business reported fourth quarter operating earnings of $96.2 million, up 30 percent from a year ago.
Improved quarterly earnings were largely driven by strong investment income, reflecting repositioning of the investment portfolio over the past year, Travelers said.
For the year, operating earnings were $359.9 million, up 28 percent.
Earnings for the year also benefited from a higher capital base, the result of reinvestment of proceeds from the sale of its MetraHealth joint venture during the fourth quarter of 1995.

Travelers Life & Annuity's earnings growth attributable to strong sales of recently introduced products, including less capital-intensive variable life insurance and annuities, was partially offset by a gradual decline in the amount of higher margin business written several years ago.

Improved sales through The Copeland Cos, Smith Barney, and a nationwide network of independent agents, reflect the company's ongoing effort to build market share by strengthening relationships in key distribution channels.
Future sales should also benefit from a recent upgrade by Standard & Poor's of Travelers Insurance Cos' claims-paying ability rating to AA-minus, Travelers said.
Deferred annuity policyholder account balances and benefit reserves rose to $13.2 billion at year-end 1996, up from $11.3 billion a year ago.
Net written premiums and deposits for the quarter were $516 million, about level with the prior year period.

Payout and group annuity balances and reserves declined to $10.9 billion at year-end 1996, compared to $12.0 billion a year ago, reflecting run-off of low margin guaranteed investment contracts written in prior years.
Net written premiums and deposits, excluding those of affiliates, fell to $238.2 million for the quarter from $325.5 million, but rose to $1.201 billion for the year from $1.085 billion in 1995.

For individual life insurance, net written premiums and deposits for the quarter increased 11 percent to $75.6 million and rose 17 percent for the year to $291.4 million, excluding Transport Life, which was spun off in September 1995.
Life insurance in force was $50.4 billion at December 31, 1996, up from $49.2 billion a year ago.
Net written premiums for the growing Long Term Care insurance line reached $34.8 million for the quarter compared to $25.1 million a year ago and $127.7 million versus $88.2 million for the year.
